scenario: Customer closes browser after OTP sent or mid-redirect
resolution: Attempt stays pending; page resumes from server state via attempt token; inquire() runs at expiry before declaring EXPIRED.

scenario: Reload or back button on OTP screen
resolution: UI reads state from server; no second INITIATE; resend obeys otp_resend_cooldown_seconds and cap.

scenario: Gateway session expires before platform TTL (10m/15m)
resolution: expires_at = min(gateway_session_ttl, platform_ttl); countdown shown; late submit rejected locally.

scenario: Repeated wrong OTP vs. brute-force attack
resolution: RETRYABLE_OTP increments otp_attempts up to max_otp_attempts (3) in AWAITING_CUSTOMER, then transitions to FAILED.

scenario: Correct OTP entered, but SUBMIT (CONFIRM) call times out
resolution: Transitions to UNKNOWN (never FAILED); same OTP is never resubmitted; slot reservation held; background reconciler polls VERIFY or statement.

scenario: Server restart or pod crash during active attempt
resolution: Durable expires_at and next_check_at in the PostgreSQL 18 database; stateless workers resume with native FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

scenario: Two browser tabs or devices open the same single-use link
resolution: Atomic active_locked_count reservation inside guard transaction; second tab sees *"Payment in progress"*.

scenario: Customer clicks retry while previous attempt is UNKNOWN
resolution: Slot reservation remains held through UNKNOWN; retry blocked server-side until UNKNOWN resolves.

scenario: Customer switches rail mid-flow (e.g., Edfali to Moamalat Card)
resolution: Old attempt cancelled via CANCEL flow (or watched until expiry); new attempt joins same attempt_group_id (success_count <= 1).

scenario: Customer approves push or scans QR after EXPIRED
resolution: Inbox stays open during grace_expires_at; verified late success transitions EXPIRED -> SUCCEEDED (or routes to refund if link already paid) and alerts ops.

scenario: Clock skew and timezone differences (Africa/Tripoli vs. UTC)
resolution: All DB timestamps UTC; format_date uses explicit gateway_timezone; webhook timestamps checked within timestamp_tolerance_sec (300s).

scenario: Link expires between checkout page load and form submit
resolution: POST /initiate re-verifies link expires_at inside serializable guard transaction and returns LINK_NOT_AVAILABLE.

scenario: Multi-use link reaches use_count while attempts are in flight
resolution: confirmed_count + active_locked_count < use_count enforced at initiation; any excess late settlement routes to SUSPENSE + refund adjustment.

scenario: POS screen hits 15-minute idle timeout while QR is pending
resolution: Attempt continues server-side; POS screen resyncs on reconnect; cashier can query by reference.

scenario: Webhook arrives before INITIATE DB transaction commits
resolution: Stored in inbound_events inbox immediately; async worker retries correlation for 60s before opening an alert.

scenario: Webhook arrives for an unknown reference
resolution: Stored in inbox with attempt_id = NULL; no state effect; volume spike alerts ops.

scenario: Duplicate webhooks delivered by gateway
resolution: Absorbed by UNIQUE(channel_id, dedupe_key) and UNIQUE(ref_type, ref_id) on journal_entries; returns idempotent 200 OK.

scenario: Out-of-order events (PAID webhook followed by late PENDING)
resolution: State machine is strictly forward-only; SUCCEEDED can never be downgraded.

scenario: Verified success arrives after attempt was marked FAILED
resolution: Transitions FAILED -> SUCCEEDED (or refund pipeline if link satisfied) and triggers P2 alert.

scenario: Verified webhook says SUCCESS, but VERIFY inquiry says FAILED
resolution: Conflicting trusted signals: nothing posted to ledger, attempt parked in UNKNOWN, P1 CONFLICT operator case opened.

scenario: Moamalat Lightbox JS completeCallback fires, but no server webhook/inquiry
resolution: Treated as hint only; attempt stays VERIFYING with backoff polling, then transitions to UNKNOWN if unconfirmed.

scenario: Attacker sends forged webhook claiming payment success
resolution: Blocked by path_token, IP CIDR allowlist, constant-time HMAC/RSA verification, and must_inquire.

scenario: Attacker replays a captured valid webhook hours later
resolution: Rejected by timestamp_tolerance_sec (300s) and 7-day dedupe_key hash in inbound_events.

scenario: Gateway retries webhook aggressively due to slow processing
resolution: Receiver stores raw event in inbound_events and returns ack_body_template in \< 10ms before async processing.

scenario: Valid webhook signature, but settled amount or currency differs
resolution: Evaluated against route mismatch_policy; held in SUSPENSE above tolerance.

scenario: Sandbox webhook sent to Live endpoint (or vice versa)
resolution: Separate path_token and secrets per environment; rejected with P2 security alert.

scenario: Gateway silently changes signature field order or algorithm
resolution: Signature-failure spike alert fires (RB-02); raw bytes preserved in inbound_events for lossless replay once new crypto_profile is approved.

scenario: Customer tampers with return_url query string (?status=success)
resolution: Return parameters are ignored for confirmation decisions; they only trigger inquire(attempt).

scenario: Callback arrives as application/x-www-form-urlencoded, XML, or non-UTF8
resolution: Channel body_format and charset normalizer parse fields while preserving raw_body_bytes for HMAC check.

scenario: Callback source IP masked by reverse proxy or changed by provider
resolution: Real IP resolved through trusted proxy hops only; valid signature from unlisted IP triggers RB-02 alert.

scenario: Gateway offers neither webhook signature nor inquiry API
resolution: Flagged HIGH_RISK; requires executive risk acceptance, mandatory statement reconciliation, and operator approval above threshold.

scenario: Settled amount differs from requested (aggregator rounding or fee)
resolution: Stored in settled_amount; governed by route mismatch_policy (HOLD_FOR_REVIEW above tolerance).

scenario: Amount scale bug (1000x too high or low on Moamalat Dirhams)
resolution: Prevented by amount_scale config, sanity bound check against link.amount, and mandatory Go-Live Gate 3 contract test.

scenario: Rail currency differs from Payment Link currency
resolution: Visible-rails formula hides any rail where rail.currency != link.currency.

scenario: Customer-borne fee (PAYER_SURCHARGE or SPLIT)
resolution: Surcharge calculated from CommissionProfile, displayed before confirmation, and booked per Section 9.1.

scenario: Customer hits personal CBL/wallet ceiling (LYPay 20k, MobiMal tier)
resolution: Mapped to canonical LIMIT_EXCEEDED; customer prompted to pick another rail; excluded from circuit-breaker failure count.

scenario: Gateway changes min/max transaction limits
resolution: Enforced on rail_routes plus optional capability-probe limit sync.

scenario: Partial payment or overpayment received
resolution: Held in SUSPENSE under mismatch_policy; resolved via Maker-Checker Adjustment.

scenario: Refund requested after refund_window_days or on no-refund rail
resolution: Blocked by rails.capabilities check; requires manual external refund + Maker-Checker Adjustment with provider_refund_ref evidence.

scenario: Upstream gateway initiates a chargeback/dispute
resolution: Webhook/statement auto-drafts a CHARGEBACK Adjustment; upon Checker approval, debits Wallet/Income and credits CHARGEBACK_RESERVE.

scenario: Second payment succeeds on a single-use link (late settlement race)
resolution: attempt_groups.success_count detects duplicate; second funds post to SUSPENSE and auto-queue refund + operator alert.

scenario: Bank/gateway statement has missing or extra lines
resolution: Reconciliation job flags MISSING_AT_GATEWAY or MISSING_LOCALLY, opens operator cases, and halts automated payouts on drift.

scenario: Gateway settles in T+N net batches (gross minus fees and refunds)
resolution: statement_sources parser supports batch net lines, matching batch reference and reconciling constituent attempts.

scenario: Gateway changes its upstream fee rate mid-month
resolution: Route cost_model is effective-dated; actual fee from statement posts difference to GATEWAY_FEE_EXPENSE as fee variance.

scenario: 3-decimal LYD link (76.255) paid on a 2-decimal gateway (76.26)
resolution: gateway_amount_wire stores "76.26"; rounding direction pinned by contract test; 0.005 variance handled by route tolerance rule.

scenario: Percentage commission calculation leaves sub-0.0001 remainder
resolution: Deterministic DECIMAL(18,4) rounding rule in CommissionProfile ensures net_merchant_amount + platform_commission_amount == amount.

scenario: Statement uploaded in Windows-1256 Arabic encoding or custom CSV delimiter
resolution: statement_sources.parser_config specifies encoding, delimiter, decimal separator, and date format, verified in Test Console preview.

scenario: Merchant on MERCHANT_DIRECT fails to pay platform commission receivable
resolution: When COMMISSION_RECEIVABLE exceeds commission_receivable_ceiling, merchant's direct routes auto-pause and balance nets against any platform-held wallet.

scenario: Primary gateway down at INITIATE (connection refused / 5xx before send)
resolution: Classified as definitive pre-point-of-no-return failure; engine transparently fails over to next ranked healthy route for that rail.

scenario: Gateway slow or flapping
resolution: Per-step AbortController timeouts + rolling gateway_health_samples transition route to DEGRADED then OPEN_BREAKER.

scenario: Scheduled bank or switch maintenance window
resolution: rail_routes.maintenance_windows hides the route proactively during the window.

scenario: Gateway retired, merged, or migrated to a new switch operator
resolution: Route set to DRAINING (in-flight attempts finish, new traffic routes elsewhere), then RETIRED preserving all historical references.

scenario: The sole route for a rail opens its circuit breaker
resolution: Rail disappears from visible_rails at checkout automatically; payment links remain valid on other rails; P1/P2 alert fires.

scenario: Aggregator (e.g., DPay) is down while direct bank gateway is up
resolution: Per-route circuit breaker isolates the aggregator route; direct route on the same rail continues serving traffic.

scenario: Both aggregator and direct routes active; customer retries across both
resolution: Both attempts share attempt_group_id; first to confirm wins; if both settle, duplicate-payment refund pipeline handles the second.

scenario: Gateway rate-limits platform (HTTP 429)
resolution: Outbound rate limiter + concurrency cap per route; READ_ONLY steps back off and retry; 429 does not trip the circuit breaker.

scenario: Gateway changes JSON response structure after a 200 OK debit
resolution: Missing required step_outputs selector on MOVES_MONEY transitions attempt to UNKNOWN (never FAILED), preserves raw text in attempt_step_logs, and pages on-call.

scenario: Route hits its daily_cap_amount
resolution: Ranker excludes the route for the remainder of the day and shifts traffic to the next active route.

scenario: Merchant enters invalid API credentials in Merchant Portal
resolution: CREDENTIAL_CHECK flow runs on save; credential set remains UNTESTED/FAILING and cannot route live traffic.

scenario: Merchant credentials expire or are revoked by the gateway
resolution: Nightly CREDENTIAL_CHECK and runtime auth errors mark set FAILING, hide its routes, alert merchant/ops, and let in-flight attempts finish.

scenario: Zero-downtime rotation of webhook or API secrets
resolution: credential_sets stores multiple active secret_version entries; verifier checks all active versions in constant time during the overlap window.

scenario: OAuth2 token refresh fails transiently at gateway
resolution: Single-flight refresh retains current valid token if unexpired, schedules jittered retry, and alerts on repeated failures (RB-05).

scenario: Two merchants attempt to register the same gateway merchant ID
resolution: Blocked by UNIQUE(gateway_id, env, external_merchant_id) on credential_sets and flagged for compliance review.

scenario: Merchant migrates from MERCHANT_DIRECT to PLATFORM_CLEARING
resolution: New credential_sets and rail_routes row activated via Maker-Checker; in-flight attempts finish on pinned set; historical ledger untouched.

scenario: Merchant suspended while payments are in flight
resolution: New attempts blocked by Guard 2; in-flight confirmed payments post to AML_HOLD / SUSPENSE per compliance policy.

scenario: Misconfiguration attempts to use Merchant A's credentials for Merchant B
resolution: Prevented by rail_routes.scope check in Ranker and hard assertion credential_set.owner_merchant_id == attempt.merchant_id in Orchestrator.

scenario: MERCHANT_DIRECT payment triggers an AML threshold hit
resolution: Platform holds no cash for direct settlement: blocks completion screen, flags merchant, and opens operational aml_cases ticket for CBL reporting.

scenario: Admin edits a gateway flow while 50 users are entering OTPs
resolution: Every payment_attempts row pins gateway_version_id at creation; all 50 in-flight attempts finish on the exact version they started with.

scenario: Defective gateway version promoted to LIVE
resolution: Gated by 12 Go-Live Gates + Canary rollout; one-click rollback restores rollback_version_id and broadcasts on InvalidationBus.

scenario: Two admins edit the same gateway concurrently
resolution: Optimistic concurrency on gateway_versions.version_number; each saves an independent draft snapshot.

scenario: Sandbox test traffic accidentally routed to Live ledger
resolution: Structural separation: env = SANDBOX attempts are rejected by LedgerPoster and excluded from all wallet/financial queries.

scenario: Gateway rejects reference format (e.g., T-LYNC 422 on duplicate, Moamalat numeric)
resolution: Per-gateway reference_format generator enforces charset/length and checks UNIQUE(reference) before sending.

scenario: Gateway brand name collision (Sadad Libya vs. KSA; Evo Wallet vs. EVO Payments)
resolution: gateways stores code, operator, country, and aliases[], displayed prominently in the Admin Wizard.

scenario: Exported gateway template imported into another environment
resolution: Exports omit all secrets by construction; imported version lands as DRAFT / UNVERIFIED requiring secret entry and CREDENTIAL_CHECK.

scenario: Maker user is unavailable or leaves company while approval is pending
resolution: Any authorized Maker can supersede the draft, and any eligible Checker (checker_user_id != maker_user_id) can review; self-approval is impossible.

scenario: Admin inspects step logs or exports config containing sensitive tokens
resolution: Multi-layer redactor scrubs secret field names and literal decrypted secret strings at write time.

scenario: Backlog of UNKNOWN attempts accumulates during switch instability
resolution: Operator Queue tracks SLA timers, supports bulk inquire(), and pages duty officer via RB-03 when age exceeds threshold.

scenario: Migrating legacy hard-coded gateway classes into the dynamic platform
resolution: Legacy classes wrap as kind = NATIVE_ADAPTER behind the 6-method contract, sharing the state machine, inbox, and LedgerPoster.

scenario: Operator tries to delete a rail or gateway with historical attempts
resolution: Hard deletion blocked by FK constraints; gateway transitions to RETIRED and rail to blocked = true.

scenario: Client POSTs modified amount or currency in /initiate or /confirm
resolution: Client request schemas have no amount field; amount is read exclusively from payment_links.amount.

scenario: Payer enters 7/9-digit card number on OTP rail
resolution: Field marked sensitivity: PAN; held in memory only for the single step, excluded from context_ciphertext and logs, gated by PCI review.

scenario: Attacker probes registered phone numbers via OTP error differences
resolution: ErrorMap normalizes subscriber-not-found and account-locked responses into a generic bilingual message.

scenario: SMS OTP pumping attack across thousands of numbers
resolution: Atomic sliding-window velocity rules per IP, link, rail, and carrier prefix + resend cooldowns block the flood.

scenario: Open redirect via payment_links.redirect_url or clickjacking on checkout
resolution: redirect_url validated against applications.redirect_domain_allowlist; checkout serves CSP: frame-ancestors 'none'.

scenario: Malicious/compromised gateway returns 100 MB payload or XML bomb
resolution: Outbound client enforces max_response_bytes (2 MB), JSON depth \<= 64, and disables XML DTD/external entities.

scenario: Customer inputs "}}<script> or \r\nX-Injected: into form field
resolution: Destination-correct encoding (JSON serializer, xml_escape, URL percent-encoding) and CR/LF rejection (Safeguard 13).

scenario: SSRF or DNS-rebinding attack via configured gateway URL
resolution: Custom DNS hook resolves and blocks private/loopback/link-local IPv4/IPv6 ranges at connection time (Safeguard 10).

scenario: Inbound webhook path_token leaked in third-party logs
resolution: Rotate path_token with overlapping validity; cryptographic signature verification still blocks unauthorized callers.

scenario: Compromised admin account attempts to reroute payouts or secrets
resolution: All credential, route, commission, and payout bank edits require four-eyes Maker-Checker approval and emit P2 security alerts.

scenario: Payer uploads executable or malware disguised as MANUAL transfer receipt
resolution: Strict magic-byte MIME check (image/png, image/jpeg, application/pdf), size cap, antivirus scan, isolated object storage with nosniff.

scenario: Customer types Arabic-Indic digits (٠٩١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨) or +218 phone prefix
resolution: rail_fields.normalizer converts Arabic-Indic digits to ASCII and normalizes phone format (09xxxxxxxx / 2189xxxxxxxx) before validation.

scenario: In-app browser (Instagram/Facebook WebView) blocks Moamalat popup/script
resolution: Checkout JS detects WebView restrictions and falls back to a REDIRECT route on the same rail or prompts *"Open in system browser"*.

scenario: Gateway returns raw Arabic/English technical error string
resolution: ErrorMap translates mapped codes to polished bilingual messages; unmapped codes show a safe generic message and log the raw code.

scenario: Customer clicks DEEP_LINK button on desktop or without wallet app installed
resolution: Checkout UI renders QR code / Pay Code alongside the deep link and falls back gracefully if app launch fails.

scenario: Cashier cancels a pending QR payment on POS terminal
resolution: Triggers CANCEL flow at gateway (if supports_cancel = true), marks attempt CANCELLED, releases link reservation, and keeps inbox open for late settlement races.

scenario: Slow upstream SMS delivery causes customer to click submit/resend repeatedly
resolution: UI disables button with live countdown; backend enforces idempotency key and otp_resend_cooldown_seconds.

scenario: Gateway confirms success, but the PostgreSQL 18 ledger insert encounters a transient lock/error
resolution: Because status transition to SUCCEEDED and LedgerPoster share one DB transaction, attempt remains in VERIFYING and worker retries posting idempotently.

scenario: Merchant webhook/notification emitted twice on retry
resolution: Outbound merchant notifications are triggered strictly from the committed journal_entries outbox with a unique event_id.

scenario: DST or timezone database update shifts gateway local timestamp formatting
resolution: format_date uses IANA tzdata (Africa/Tripoli); contract tests assert two fixed historical instants per gateway version.

scenario: Duplicate webhook redelivered across a worker pod restart (after DB commit, before HTTP ack)
resolution: inbound_events dedupe key and UNIQUE(ref_type, ref_id) on journal_entries guarantee zero double-posting across restarts.

scenario: Finance approves a REFUND adjustment while customer starts a new attempt on a multi-use link
resolution: Refund Adjustment locks and references the specific source_attempt_id, operating independently of new attempts on the link.

scenario: Gateway silently reorders or renames columns in daily CSV/XLSX settlement statement
resolution: statement_sources parser validates header row against required column map; halts ingest and fires P2 alert on schema drift.

scenario: Route paused or credential rotated on Node A while Node B serves checkout traffic
resolution: InvalidationBus (Redis Pub/Sub) evicts Node B caches in \< 1s; attempt initiation always verifies route/version state against the PostgreSQL 18 database.

scenario: Gateway incident unleashes 10,000 webhook retries in 60 seconds
resolution: Inbox receiver performs lightweight insert + ack; bounded worker queue drains inbound_events with per-route concurrency caps.

scenario: POS tablet loses Wi-Fi/cellular connectivity mid-payment
resolution: Attempt completes server-side; on reconnect, POS screen replays missed state from /v1/pay/{linkKey}/logs/{logId}/status.

scenario: Clock drift between platform cluster and gateway exceeds tolerance
resolution: NTP sync monitored via alert; inbound timestamp rejection triggers RB-02 while preserving raw event in inbound_events for replay.

scenario: Admin accidentally configures a static reusable QR code across attempts
resolution: Save-time validator requires QR/Pay-Code INITIATE flows to bind ATTEMPT.gateway_reference or dynamic session output.

scenario: Rolling deployment runs two application versions simultaneously
resolution: Both app versions execute the attempt's pinned gateway_version_id snapshot using the deterministic closed transform library.

scenario: Route set to DRAINING or Credential Set marked REVOKED with attempts in flight
resolution: Pinned route_id and credential_set_id allow in-flight AWAITING_CUSTOMER / VERIFYING attempts to finish; only new attempts re-rank.

scenario: Automated settlement sweep runs at the exact moment a late payment confirms
resolution: Row-level locking on the gl_accounts checkpoint and explicit reconciliation_items matching serialize the sweep cleanly.

scenario: Merchant edits payout_bank_details_json while a cashout_requests row is PROCESSING
resolution: cashout_requests snapshots destination_bank_json at request creation; subsequent edits require Maker-Checker and apply only to future payouts.

scenario: Aggregator (e.g., MyPay/DPay) renames an underlying payment method alias
resolution: Nightly CREDENTIAL_CHECK capability probe detects missing alias, marks route DEGRADED, and alerts integration engineering.

scenario: Two partial refund Adjustments approved concurrently for the same attempt
resolution: Execution serializes via SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on payment_attempts and asserts SUM(executed_refunds) + new_refund <= settled_amount.

scenario: Gateway returns a non-unique provider_reference across two different attempts
resolution: Correlation prioritizes our_reference (gateway_reference); provider_reference-only correlation scopes by (gateway_id, env, amount, active_window) and flags collisions to operator_cases.

scenario: Prolonged power/internet outage across a merchant's physical store POS fleet
resolution: All state and timers reside on the server; expired POS links release reservations cleanly; settled payments credit the merchant wallet regardless of screen connectivity.

scenario: Applicant abandons a DRAFT join request after uploading documents
resolution: Draft moves to EXPIRED after 30 inactive days; uploaded documents remain encrypted, are excluded from reviewer queues, and are purged by the retention job; the applicant can start a new request.

scenario: A Google sign-in presents an e-mail identical to an existing password-based account
resolution: No auto-link. The user must authenticate to the existing account with a second factor before the Google sub is attached; otherwise a separate identity is created and flagged by duplicate detection.

scenario: A rejected applicant re-applies under a new trade name, phone number and e-mail
resolution: Duplicate detection matches tax ID, registration number, owner national ID, payout bank account, device fingerprint or document hash; the request is forced to four-eyes, risk tier is raised one level, and prior records are shown to the reviewer.

scenario: An admin-assisted onboarding is prepared by the same operator who is assigned to decide it
resolution: The person who prepared the request on behalf of the applicant is recorded as maker and is barred from the deciding-reviewer and checker roles for that request.

scenario: The same KYB document hash appears under two unrelated merchants
resolution: Both requests receive a DUPLICATE_DOCUMENT flag; reviewers must justify acceptance; repeated reuse across merchants opens an AML case against the submitting identities.

scenario: Beneficial owners are added or changed between submission and decision
resolution: A new screening is triggered for the changed owner; the request returns to IN_REVIEW; any pending approval is invalidated and must be re-submitted.

scenario: Arabic name variants (diacritics, transliterations) cause a missed sanctions hit or a flood of false positives
resolution: Names are normalized and sent in Arabic and Latin forms; score thresholds are tuned against a fixed Arabic test set required by the compliance readiness checklist; reviewers see scores and may suppress confirmed false positives with an expiry.

scenario: A watch-list update creates a new match on an already-active merchant
resolution: A LIST_UPDATE screening opens a case, restricts cash-out immediately, and keeps payment acceptance unless severity is CRITICAL, in which case the merchant is emergency-suspended and ratified within 24 h.

scenario: The screening provider is unavailable during onboarding
resolution: The screening result is ERROR; approval is impossible (fail-closed); the request stays IN_REVIEW, retries run with backoff, the SLA is paused with reason PROVIDER_OUTAGE, and the incident is visible on the compliance dashboard.

scenario: A merchant splits one large sale across several links, applications or rails to stay under an AML threshold
resolution: Rules aggregate by subject (merchant, beneficial owner, payer identifier) over the window, not by link or application; the STRUCTURING rule flags many payments clustered just under the threshold and opens a case.

scenario: A voluntary refund was issued and a chargeback arrives later for the same payment
resolution: The dispute is linked to the refund; execution asserts SUM(executed refunds) + chargeback <= settled_amount under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (as in Edge Case 113); the chargeback Adjustment is capped to the not-yet-returned amount.

scenario: An emergency suspension is never ratified within 24 hours
resolution: A P2 alert and an escalation to MLRO fire; the suspension stays in force (fail-safe); it is never auto-reversed; the request remains open until ratified or replaced by a standard reinstatement approval.

scenario: A dispute webhook is replayed, or a statement containing the same chargeback is re-imported
resolution: UNIQUE(gateway_id, external_dispute_ref) and the inbox dedupe key absorb the duplicate; no second Adjustment is drafted.

scenario: An AML hold is approved for release while the merchant is SUSPENDED or requesting closure
resolution: The ledger resolution executes regardless of merchant state (accounting is independent of lifecycle); closure is refused while any hold, reserve, open dispute or non-zero balance exists.

scenario: Support staff or a merchant asks why an account was restricted for AML reasons
resolution: The response is the generic notice; AML data is not exposed to SUPPORT or merchants; the request itself is logged; there is no tipping-off.

scenario: The entered NeomPay wallet ID fails the check-digit test or has an unknown type code
resolution: Rejected at field validation with a generic bilingual message; no call is made to NeomPay; the failure counts toward per-IP velocity so the check cannot be used to enumerate wallets.

scenario: The payer's wallet is frozen, closed or restricted in NeomPay
resolution: ErrorMap classifies as TERMINAL_DECLINE with a generic customer message; it does not count toward the circuit breaker (a customer condition, not a gateway fault).

scenario: The NeomPay ledger times out or is unavailable
resolution: On a MOVES_MONEY step the attempt becomes UNKNOWN and holds the link slot; idempotent retry and inquire(attempt) resolve it; the route moves to DEGRADED / OPEN_BREAKER and other rails remain offered.

scenario: The payer wallet belongs to the same legal entity as the merchant (self-payment)
resolution: SELF_PAYMENT_POLICY (default BLOCK) creates a terminal BLOCKED attempt; alternative FLAG_AND_ALLOW opens an AML case; prevents wash volume and artificial commission.

scenario: NeomPay captured the payer's funds but the platform crashed before committing the journal entry
resolution: On restart the sweeper runs inquire(attempt), finds a captured payment, and posts the entry idempotently; UNIQUE(ref_type, ref_id) prevents a second posting; the daily cross-ledger check would expose any miss.

scenario: The payer approves a push request after the attempt has expired
resolution: NeomPay-side request TTL equals the attempt's expires_at; a late capture is rejected. If a capture slipped through, State Machine Rule 6 (late-success recovery) applies, with funds in SUSPENSE and an auto-drafted refund if the link slot is gone.

scenario: The customer double-taps the OTP submit button or the browser retries the request
resolution: The deterministic Idempotency-Key (gateway_reference) returns the same result; at most one debit occurs; the second request is a read of the first.

scenario: The payer wallet's type is not allowed to pay merchants
resolution: The type-code allow-list on the rail field rejects it at validation with a neutral message; no money moves.

scenario: A refund is approved but the payer's NeomPay wallet has since been closed
resolution: The REFUND step fails; the Adjustment stays EXECUTING and an operator case opens; FINANCE may complete the return by another channel with evidence under Maker-Checker, or, after the policy period, reclassify the funds to SUSPENSE as unclaimed.

scenario: The daily cross-ledger equality check (NeomPay ledger export versus Treasury inflows from NeomPay) shows drift
resolution: Runbook RB-04 applies: automated payouts of NeomPay-sourced funds halt, a MISMATCH operator case is opened, and the daily job is re-run; no manual ledger edits are allowed; the correction is a Maker-Checker Adjustment.
